item.title: iCloud Private Relay might be leaking your real IP address, researchers say
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 6.18
Security researchers have discovered a problem with Apple’s iCloud Private Relay service. While the feature is meant to protect your real IP address, it might actually be leaking it to websites. A new iCloud Private Relay problem This iCloud Private Relay vulnerability was discovered by security researchers Tommy Mysk and Talal Haj Bakry, who detailed the problem in-depth on their website. “In short: any website that supports, or pretends to support, passkeys can see the user’s real IP address despite having iCloud Private Relay on,” they say. As a refresher, iCloud Private Relay is not a VPN. As we’ve explained before, it only protects your IP address in Safari, whereas VPNs protect all traffic from your device by running at the system level. As 404 Media explains, the problem is due to a series of issues in Apple’s WebKit engine and how it handles passkeys. In a quirk of how passkeys work — a broadly secure alternative to usernames and passwords which use the WebAuthn standard — a user’s device makes a web request outside of the browser itself. Meaning, that request essentially bypasses Private Relay and exposes a user’s real IP address, even though to them it may look like they are simply interacting with a website as normal. “Because the fetch is issued by the operating system’s credential service rather than by Safari, it never enters Private Relay’s proxied path. The destination server sees the device’s real IP address either way,” the researchers write in their research. The impact of the problem is worsened on iOS, where all browsers are required to use Apple’s WebKit engine (in most countries): Because all web browsers on iOS have to use Apple’s WebKit engine, the researchers also found the issues impact at least one Tor browser, called OnionBrowser. The Tor anonymity network routes users’ traffic through multiple nodes located all over the world. But some of the newly discovered issues can expose their IP address too. Mysk says they reported the problem to the Tor Project, which said it was “dire.” Nonetheless, the company reportedly didn’t provide a timeline on when the problem will be fixed, but agreed to let Mysk disclose it anyway. Mysk also filed a security report with Apple, the status of which currently says a fix is planned for Fall 2026: “We’re planning to address the issue you reported.” You can check whether the problem impacts you via a website set up by the security researchers. Today’s report follows a separate bug impacting Apple’s Hide My Email feature. This vulnerability, which allowed anyone to access a user’s real email address, was fixed by Apple last month. item.title: Apple’s latest macOS updates address a serious Screen Sharing vulnerability
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 6.02
Apple has now published the security details for today’s macOS Tahoe, Sequoia, and Sonoma updates, revealing that all three address a serious Screen Sharing vulnerability. Here is what Apple fixed. Apple addresses Screen Sharing vulnerability Earlier today, Apple released macOS Sonoma 14.8.9, macOS Sequoia 15.7.9, and macOS Tahoe 26.6.1, with the release notes for all three saying only that they provided “important security fixes” and were recommended for all users. Apple has now updated its security releases page with details of the vulnerability addressed by the updates. Across all three versions of macOS, Apple fixed a bug that could allow “an attacker on the network” to “authenticate to Screen Sharing without valid credentials.” Here’s the full security note: Screen Sharing Available for: macOS Tahoe [macOS Sequoia, macOS Sonoma] Impact: An attacker on the network may be able to authenticate to Screen Sharing without valid credentials Description: An authentication issue was addressed with improved state management. CVE-2026-65400: Alfredo Pesoli (@__rev) via Bynario Atlas (bynar.io) While there is no indication that the bug was exploited in the wild, Apple’s description suggests that an attacker could bypass Screen Sharing’s authentication checks and remotely access a vulnerable Mac. Depending on the system’s configuration and the privileges granted to the session, this could allow them to view the screen, open apps and files, or perform other actions on the Mac. Even if you don’t use Screen Sharing, it may be a good idea to install the update sooner rather than later, given that Apple deemed the vulnerability serious enough to patch across three versions of macOS without prior beta testing or waiting for its next major round of OS updates. To learn more bout Apple’s security updates, follow this link. Comments

item.title: iPhone 18 Pro event date: When Apple announced its event over the last six years
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 5.82
When should we expect the iPhone 18 Pro event, and when will Apple officially announce the date? Apple hasn’t sent invitations yet, but its announcement history gives us a remarkably consistent window. Apple’s iPhone event announcement dates: 2020–2025 Apple has announced its annual iPhone event two weeks in advance for four consecutive years. Here’s when Apple announced each of its last six iPhone events, plus what those dates suggest for September 2026. | Model | Event announcement | Event date | Delta | |---|---|---|---| | iPhone 17 | Tuesday, August 26, 2025 | Tuesday, September 9, 2025 | 14 days | | iPhone 16 | Monday, August 26, 2024 | Monday, September 9, 2024 | 14 days | | iPhone 15 | Tuesday, August 29, 2023 | Tuesday, September 12, 2023 | 14 days | | iPhone 14 | Wednesday, August 24, 2022 | Wednesday, September 7, 2022 | 14 days | | iPhone 13 | Tuesday, September 7, 2021 | Tuesday, September 14, 2021 | 7 days | | iPhone 12 | Tuesday, October 6, 2020 | Tuesday, October 13, 2020 | 7 days | The pandemic disrupted Apple’s regular iPhone event schedule in 2020 and 2021. The iPhone 12 event moved to October, and Apple provided only seven days’ notice for both the iPhone 12 and iPhone 13 events. Since 2022, however, Apple has been remarkably consistent. Every iPhone event has been announced exactly 14 days before the presentation. When is the iPhone 18 Pro / iPhone Ultra event? Apple hasn’t officially announced the next iPhone event date, but Wednesday, September 9, is currently the leading possibility. Apple offered its first official clue this week when it opened applications for US retail employees to work its Event Support Experience Program in California. The company told employees that the event will occur during the first half of September. Bloomberg suggests that Wednesday appears slightly more likely because Labor Day falls on Monday, September 7. A Wednesday event would preserve the workday travel window Apple has historically provided attendees. When will Apple announce the new iPhone event? If Apple holds its event on September 9 and maintains its four-year pattern, it would announce the date exactly two weeks earlier on Wednesday, August 26. That makes August 26 the strongest prediction for Apple’s iPhone 18 event invitation. Tuesday, August 25, remains another possibility, but it would create a 15-day gap rather than continuing Apple’s recent 14-day pattern. What to expect at Apple’s September 2026 event This year’s product lineup should make the event unusually significant. Apple is expected to unveil three new flagship iPhones: iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and its first foldable iPhone, possibly called iPhone Ultra. Noticeably absent will be the standard iPhone 18. Apple is expected to split its release schedule beginning this cycle, saving iPhone 18, iPhone 18e, and iPhone Air 2 for spring 2027. September is also when Apple traditionally unveils new Apple Watch hardware. AirPods sometimes join the presentation as well, although they aren’t guaranteed to receive annual updates. The event will mark another first for Apple. John Ternus becomes CEO on September 1, while Tim Cook moves to executive chairman of the board. That will make this the first iPhone event of the Ternus era. Do more with your Apple products Comments

item.title: Meta launches Muse Code AI coding agent for macOS and Linux
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 5.82
Meta is entering the AI coding-agent race with Muse Code, a new terminal-based tool now available in beta for macOS and Linux. Muse Code arrives alongside Meta’s new Muse Spark 1.2 model Powered by the new Muse Spark 1.2 model, it is designed to handle complex software engineering work across large repositories. For Mac users, Muse Code installation is a one-line command: curl -fsSL https://dev.meta.ai/install.sh | bash Unlike ChatGPT Codex and Claude Code, there’s currently no dedicated app interface for Muse Code. Meta says Muse Code can plan changes, write code, validate its work, and coordinate persistent background agents that remain active throughout a session. Its local event log records model calls, tool use, approvals, and edits, allowing work to resume after a crash. Built-in commands can also generate a plan, stress-test it, or continue working toward a specified goal. Muse Spark 1.2 is described as a coding-focused update with gains in code generation, debugging, codebase understanding, and long-running developer workflows. The model is available through both Muse Code and the Meta Model API with expanded global access. The release follows Meta’s July launch of Muse Spark 1.1, which upgraded the model’s agentic and multimodal abilities and introduced Meta’s paid API service for developers. Before that, Meta replaced Llama with the original Muse Spark in April, then used it to expand the Meta AI app and power new image-generation features across Meta’s apps. Do more with your Apple products Comments

item.title: iOS 27 basically turns your iPhone and AirPods into an Apple Watch at the gym
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 5.82
GymKit has been one of Apple Watch’s smartest fitness features since it launched in 2017. Tap your watch to compatible gym equipment, and Apple Watch shares your heart rate while the machine sends back metrics like distance, incline, pace, and calories. With iOS 27, Apple is expanding that idea beyond Apple Watch. I tested the new GymKit on iPhone and AirPods Pro 3 experience with a GymKit-compatible treadmill. It basically gives you the Apple Watch GymKit workout tracking experience, just without the watch. This could be useful in a lot of scenarios. GymKit, no Apple Watch required The setup is simple. I tapped my iPhone to the treadmill, picked Indoor Walk (Indoor Run is also offered), and started the workout from the treadmill. With GymKit, workout data is stored privately on iPhone and removed from the equipment. Once the workout started, the treadmill received heart-rate data from AirPods Pro 3. Meanwhile, the Fitness app on iPhone received the treadmill’s distance, pace, incline, and calorie data. Treadmills know details that an iPhone and AirPods can’t know on their own, especially incline and precise belt distance. As a side note: Apple Watch has more accurate treadmill workout tracking as part of watchOS 27. GymKit remains the gold standard for accurate data, though. GymKit also avoids two awkward gym habits. You don’t need to hold the treadmill’s metal heart-rate contacts while jogging. You also do not need to wear a Bluetooth heart-rate strap. AirPods Pro 3 become the heart-rate source (and likely your podcast or music audio source as well). iPhone becomes the workout computer, which you can monitor during your workout. And the treadmill fills in the machine data while providing the surface for walking or running. iPhone and AirPods have become more like an Apple Watch Apple has been moving more fitness features onto iPhone for years. iOS first made the Fitness app useful without Apple Watch as Apple Fitness+ leaned into iPhone as an entry point. AirPods Pro 3 pushed that further as the first AirPods with heart-rate tracking, after Apple tested the idea with Powerbeats Pro 2. iOS 27 brings those pieces together. GymKit on iPhone shouldn’t replace Apple Watch for people who wear one every day. Instead, it’s a great backup when your Apple Watch is dead, charging, or left at home. It also gives iPhone and AirPods users a taste of the Apple Watch experience, which could attract future Apple Watch customers. In testing with iOS 27 beta 1, my Exercise ring didn’t update as I worked out without wearing Apple Watch. But after I put my watch back on, the Exercise ring caught up, and the workout appeared in Fitness with the right data. My sample 16-minute treadmill walk showed 0.66 miles, 65 active calories, 97 total calories, 32 feet of elevation gain, and a 115 BPM average heart rate, just like if I’d worn an Apple Watch. If I tried to use GymKit on iPhone without AirPods, the iPhone disconnected when the workout started because it had no heart-rate source. If I tried to start GymKit from iPhone while wearing Apple Watch, iOS pointed me back to the Workout app on Apple Watch instead, though you can continue without using the watch. AirPods heart-rate permission also matters. You can manage it in Settings under your AirPods settings and privacy options. I had turned it off, mostly as a theoretical battery-saving move, but this test convinced me to turn it back on. AirPods Pro 3 can also work with Apple Watch to provide the best available heart-rate data. GymKit on iPhone with AirPods is a great addition to Apple’s Fitness ecosystem GymKit on iPhone is one of those iOS 27 features that sounds small until it solves a real problem. If Apple Watch is your default workout tracker, it probably stays that way. But if your watch dies or you forget it at home, iPhone plus AirPods Pro 3 can now log a treadmill workout with real heart-rate data and real treadmill metrics. That’s a neat upgrade, and it makes Apple’s broader Fitness strategy feel more complete. Do more with your Apple products Comments

item.title: GPT-5 turning one as OpenAI shares new Agent Plugins standard
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 5.78
OpenAI’s GPT-5 turns one tomorrow, and the company is marking the week by looking beyond individual models. Today, OpenAI introduced Agent Plugins, an open standard meant to let reusable AI-agent extensions work across compatible products. GPT-5’s first year GPT-5 launched August 7, 2025, replacing GPT-4o and several reasoning models as ChatGPT’s default. Its defining feature was automatic routing: ChatGPT could answer quickly or invoke deeper reasoning depending on the request. OpenAI also claimed fewer factual errors than GPT-4o. Apple adopted the model with iOS 26, iPadOS 26, and macOS Tahoe 26. ChatGPT requests passed through Apple Intelligence, including Siri handoffs, Writing Tools, and visual intelligence, switched from GPT-4o to GPT-5. GPT-5.1 promised warmer, more natural answers in November. December’s “code red” GPT-5.2 accelerated professional work in response to Gemini. GPT-5.3 Instant targeted ChatGPT’s “cringe” tone, followed two days later by GPT-5.4 Thinking with a million-token context window and built-in computer use. OpenAI subsequently added GPT-5.4 mini and nano, the restricted GPT-5.4-Cyber, GPT-5.5 for more autonomous work, GPT-5.5 Instant, and July’s GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna models. From the Codex Mac app to a new ChatGPT The software around those models transformed too. OpenAI launched a dedicated Codex Mac app in February as a hub for running multiple coding agents, reviewing changes, and scheduling work. In July, Codex effectively became the new ChatGPT desktop app, combining Chat, Work, and Codex while the previous native client was renamed ChatGPT Classic. For me, Codex has changed how I work with ChatGPT the most. I’m able to offload a lot more work that doesn’t require critical thinking and even build tools on my Mac that I couldn’t put together otherwise. OpenAI introduces Agent Plugins Next, OpenAI is introducing Agent Plugins that offer a portable package format for bundling skills and MCP servers. Agent Plugins is an open, vendor-neutral standard for packaging reusable components into portable plugins. Its version 1.0.0 specification defines a shared format for Agent Skills and MCP servers that compatible clients can discover and load consistently. Per the Agent Plugins site, the technology is “openly licensed and developed in public.” The vendor-neutral project’s steering committee includes Amazon, Cursor, Microsoft, OpenAI, and Vercel. When is GPT-6 coming? OpenAI has not announced GPT-6. The clearest clue is Astra, an unreleased model family. OpenAI recently said an internal version advanced 10 longstanding math and computer-science problems, but the company has not called Astra GPT-6. Release timing may no longer be OpenAI’s decision alone. GPT-5.6’s public rollout was briefly held back for US government security review. Astra could be close without being imminent. It could also arrive under yet another GPT-5 name. However it goes, tomorrow marks one year with GPT-5, and for me, the arrival of Codex as an agentic tool has changed my use the most, year-over-year. Do more with your Apple products Comments

item.title: MacPaw is building an on-device AI layer that will work across your Mac apps
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 5.77
MacPaw has announced a long-term strategic partnership with Liquid AI to co-develop an on-device AI technology stack built specifically for the Mac. The collaboration will start with Eney, MacPaw’s AI assistant for macOS. MacPaw is teaming up with Liquid AI to bring more on-device AI to the Mac Liquid AI’s Liquid Foundation Models (LFMs) will be adapted for Mac-based assistance and combined with MacPaw’s own on-device technologies: Mnemos for memory and Elix for inference. Eney already shifted to a local model last year, keeping reasoning, contextual search, skill execution, and conversation history on the device whenever possible. The new partnership is intended to push that approach further. The two companies are jointly developing the underlying stack rather than MacPaw simply adding another third-party model. Once the technology has been tested and implemented in Eney, MacPaw says it plans to bring it to more of its products. It also wants to make the shared AI stack available to Mac developers through Setapp. That could let participating apps expose more of their capabilities and context to Eney. This would allow the assistant to understand what is inside an app. It could also provide more useful answers or take relevant actions. You can learn more about MacPaw’s on-device AI technology and today’s announcement here, and catch up on Liquid AI here. Do more with your Apple products Comments

item.title: Apple holds 65% of the premium smartphone market as segment reaches record high
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 5.67
Counterpoint Research says Apple captured 65% of the premium smartphone market in the first half of 2026, as the segment grew to a record 29% of global smartphone sales. Here are the details. iPhone 17 helps Apple reverse last year’s decline In a new report, Counterpoint Research said premium smartphones ($600 and up) accounted for a record 29% of the overall market during the first half of 2026, up four percentage points year-over-year. From that total, Apple accounted for 65% of premium smartphone sales, up from 63% in H1 2025 but down from 74% in H1 2022. Samsung held steady at 19% compared with last year, up from 17% in 2022. Counterpoint attributed Apple’s 9% year-over-year growth to the strong performance of the iPhone 17 line, “especially the base model,” reversing last year’s downturn it says was the result of “intensified competition in China.” Here’s Counterpoint Research’s Senior Analyst Harshit Rastogi on the report: Rising memory and component costs are reshaping smartphone pricing and creating opportunities for OEMs to accelerate premiumization. As mid-segment Android smartphone prices rise, the price gap with premium devices, especially older or discounted flagship models, is narrowing. This trend makes flagship smartphones a better upgrade option for consumers. To support this shift, OEMs are expanding financing, trade-in and buyback programs to improve affordability. Samsung has also expanded its Galaxy Forever program to several markets to make flagship devices more accessible.” Counterpoint notes that brands have been “pushing premium smartphones through trade-in, financing and buyback programs,” adding that “premiumisation is expected to continue due to better component procurement, consistent demand and financing.” To read Counerpoint’s full report, follow this link. Comments

item.title: Report shares new pricing and design details about OpenAI’s first device
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 5.53
After sharing initial details about OpenAI’s plans for its first smart device, Bloomberg has published a new report with more information about its form factor and price. Here are the details. OpenAI’s speaker may cost upwards of $300 A few weeks ago, Bloomberg reported that OpenAI’s first device would be a battery-powered portable speaker equipped with a camera and other sensors, as well as “mechanical elements that can move on their own, creating a sense that it is alive and not just an object responding to commands.” The report said OpenAI was developing “roughly five different products” but planned to begin with the speaker, which it hoped to unveil this year ahead of a 2027 release. The publication added that this timeline, however, could change depending on the outcome of Apple’s lawsuit accusing OpenAI of using trade secrets stolen by former Apple employees to develop its upcoming hardware products. Now, Bloomberg has shared new details about OpenAI’s plans for its first device, reporting that the company has discussed pricing it between $300 and $400 per unit. The product is expected to have a “premium look,” use “upscale materials like high-quality metal,” and remain in use throughout the day. From the report: The product — essentially a smart speaker without a display — will be shaped like a doughnut that’s roughly the size of a hockey puck. (…) And the design should help it stand out from current smart speakers, a category dominated by Amazon.com Inc. and Alphabet Inc.’s Google. Bloomberg adds that the speaker “will be designed to work in different positions,” including in the user’s hand or on furniture around the house. Its moving parts are intended to make it feel more alive, while more advanced AI models will support natural, humanlike voice interactions similar to ChatGPT’s recently revamped voice mode. Today’s report comes on the same day that OpenAI filed a motion to dismiss Apple’s lawsuit. The company argues that Apple failed to identify specific trade secrets or plausibly allege that OpenAI engaged in improper conduct, saying the complaint framed “ordinary conduct” out of context and was “filed without adequate investigation.” As Bloomberg notes in today’s report, the reported form factor “is not something Apple has come close to launching,” although its use of premium metal could relate to one of the manufacturing allegations in Apple’s lawsuit. Bloomberg cautions that it remains unclear whether that allegation concerns this device, another product, or a discarded concept. To read Bloomberg’s full report, follow this link. Comments

item.title: iOS 27 adds four new ways to customize your iPhone’s Lock Screen
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 5.52
iOS 27 continues Apple’s trend of giving you more control over the design of your iPhone’s Lock Screen. This year, there are new customization options, wallpaper settings, and more. Extend wallpapers iOS 27 brings new Apple Intelligence editing features to the Photos app. This includes a revamped version of Clean Up, as well as a Reframe. Another new option is Extend, which intelligently expands your image so you can adjust its aspect ratio, straighten horizons, or just add more space around the edges. As seen above, the Extend feature also comes to the Lock Screen in iOS 27. If a photo doesn’t match your iPhone’s aspect ratio or isn’t cropped quite right for a wallpaper, iOS 27 will automatically suggest using Extend to fix it. Extend will use AI to generate additional image content around the edges, so you have more flexibility when setting a picture as your iPhone’s wallpaper. Generate your own wallpapers iOS 27 brings big improvements to Image Playground, which is Apple’s app that lets you generate images using artificial intelligence. The changes to Image Playground also come to your iPhone’s Lock Screen. Now, you can generate wallpapers using Image Playground right from the wallpaper picker in Settings or on the Lock Screen itself. In the wallpaper picker, you’ll see a new “Image Playground” option. The feature will create stylized versions of images from your Photos library, such as “Retro Illustration” and “Animation.” You can also create a custom wallpaper from scratch just by describing what you want in natural language. Move the clock iOS 27 finally lets you shrink the clock on your iPhone’s Lock Screen. While Apple has let you customize the clock’s size for several years, iOS 27 goes a step further. Now, you can move the clock on your Lock Screen up to the top row of widgets. This frees up space on your Lock Screen so you can see more of your wallpaper. It does, of course, come at the expense of being able to glance at the time from far away. For many people, though, the point of the Lock Screen is to show off wallpapers, and iOS 27 makes that even easier. Swipe away the Now Playing widget With iOS 27, you can now swipe away the Now Playing widget that appears on your iPhone’s Lock Screen. Even if you clear the Now Playing widget, whatever you’re listening to will continue playing. This is great if you find yourself accidentally tapping the Now Playing widget on your Lock Screen. Wrap up iOS 27 is currently available to developers and public beta testers. It will be released to everyone later this year. What do you think of the new Lock Screen customization features in iOS 27? Let us know down in the comments. Chance’s favorites: Follow Chance: Threads, Bluesky, Instagram, and Mastodon. Comments

item.title: Security Bite: Apple’s baffling bug bounty changes finally make sense
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 5.52
9to5Mac Security Bite is exclusively brought to you by Mosyle, the only Apple Unified Platform. Making Apple devices work-ready and enterprise-safe is all we do. Our unique integrated approach to management and security combines state-of-the-art Apple-specific security solutions for fully automated Hardening & Compliance, Next Generation EDR, AI-powered Zero Trust, and exclusive Privilege Management with the most powerful and modern Apple MDM on the market. The result is a totally automated Apple Unified Platform currently trusted by over 45,000 organizations to make millions of Apple devices work-ready with no effort and at an affordable cost. Request your EXTENDED TRIAL today and understand why Mosyle is everything you need to work with Apple. Apple dropped a staggering number of vulnerability patches in macOS Tahoe 26.6 last month. Plus a heap of fixes in iOS 26.6 and iPadOS 26.6. What stood out most to me was the number of credits that went to Claude, Codex, and other AI-adjacent tools and labs. The most I’ve ever seen in a single release. Then came this week when Apple confirmed that it has capped the number of vulnerability reports a researcher can have open at once, with a 30-day cool-off period once that cap is reached. On the surface, it looks like Apple got caught flat-footed here and started throwing up walls. It even admitted to “the growing volume of AI-generated security submissions across the industry” in its statement to the Financial Times. However, it’s now increasingly clear that, since last year, nearly all of Apple’s rather baffling decisions around its security bug bounty program have been in preparation for this exact problem. The changes really started in October 2025, when Apple announced what it called a “major evolution” of the Apple Security Bounty program. The headlines then boasted the program’s new $2 million top prize, which could climb north of $5 million with bonuses. Buried in the same announcement was a new Capture the Flag-like system called Target Flags, built for bug hunters to better prove the depth of an exploit. Reports submitted with Target Flags can be processed programmatically, meaning they can be validated without a human reviewer. For the researcher, this means a faster payday. Awards could be processed as soon as the bug is received and verified, even before a patch ships. In hindsight, this was the first clear sign of Apple preparing for a wave of AI-generated reports. With Target Flags, it could split submissions into those that already prove their severity and those that need a human to sit down and check. Then two months later, things got baffling when the floor fell out on a lot of low-hanging fruit. In December 2025, Csaba Fitzl, principal macOS security researcher at Iru, spotted a massive change in the allotted award amounts. Full TCC bypasses had dropped from $30.5k to $5k. Individual TCC categories fell from the $5k to $10k range down to $1k. macOS sandbox escapes were halved to $5k. At the time, 9to5Mac verified every one of them against Apple’s own bounty categories page. Fitzl warned that few researchers focus on the Mac to begin with, and that smaller awards would shrink that number further while raising the odds that whoever finds an exploit sells it on the black market instead of reporting it. At the time, it baffled everyone, myself included. Apple was suddenly paying more for the incredibly rare and spectacular exploit chains and less for the everyday macOS patches that make up most of what lands in release notes. Then June arrived with the cap on open reports and the 30-day cool-off, which apparently nobody knew about until this week, aside from the researchers who ran into it. When piecing this timeline together and these three recent moves, two of which felt disconnected and honestly a little hostile at the time, it now clearly looks like a coordinated response. TCC bypasses and sandbox escapes are precisely the class of bug that AI-assisted tooling (like Claude Fable) is best at surfacing right now. It’s shallow enough to find at scale, common enough to bury a triage queue, and every single one still needs a human at Apple to look at it. Paying less here and far more for the deep exploit chains that still demand real expertise, now makes way more sense. To be clear, I don’t want to knock researchers who use AI. The 26.6 release notes are proof that these tools are finding real, exploitable, patchable bugs across Apple’s ecosystem. As I said on X, AI-assisted or not, credit where credits due. This benefits everyone. The problem was never AI-assisted research. It’s what happens when a bounty program built around human-paced submissions meets machine output at an insane scale. As things become clearer, something tells me this is just the start of the bug bounty program’s AI growing pains. Security Bite is 9to5Mac’s weekly deep dive into the world of Apple security. Each week, Arin Waichulis unpacks new threats, privacy concerns, vulnerabilities, and more, shaping an ecosystem of over 2 billion devices. Every other week on the Security Bite Podcast, he sits down with experts in the field to break down the most pressing topics. Follow Arin: Twitter/X, LinkedIn, Threads Comments

item.title: Abode launches new Apple Home-compatible sensors for garages, gates, more
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 5.40
DIY smart home security company Abode expanded its Apple Home-compatible lineup today with two new sensors designed to monitor garage doors, gates, sheds, and other entry points. Here are the details. Abode announces two Apple Home-compatible sensors Abode today announced its new Garage Tilt Sensor and Outdoor Contact Sensor, designed to monitor entry points that the company says are often beyond the reach of traditional indoor sensors. Both products are compatible with Apple Home, as well as with Alexa and Google Assistant. They can leverage Abode’s CUE smart home automation engine to offer personalized behaviors, such as “driveway lights that switch on the moment an entry gate opens after dark, or a garage door that closes itself if it’s been left open for more than 10 minutes,” according to the company. Here’s Abode on its new wireless Garage Tilt Sensor, which the company says offers up to 10 years of battery life: The Garage Tilt Sensor detects motion by sensing when a surface changes orientation more than 45° from its resting position in either direction, making it ideal for up-and-over-style or tilt-style garage doors, attic hatch doors, basement tilt windows, and any hinged panel that swings open at an angle. Homeowners receive an alert in the Abode app if the sensor is triggered, like when a garage door begins to open or close. As for Abode’s new IP66-rated Outdoor Contact Sensor, the company says: The Outdoor Contact Sensor is purpose-built for metal gates, sheds, storage units, mailboxes and detached garages. A stronger magnet and wider activation gap reduce the false alarms that plague indoor sensors used outside. When triggered, the mid-size sensor will immediately notify users through the Abode app, allowing them to respond quickly to unexpected activity. Abode says that under “optimal conditions,” connectivity with both sensors can extend up to 500 feet, adding that its easy-to-follow setup instructions guide lets users test the range before mounting. Here’s Chris Carney, CEO and Founder of Abode, on today’s announcements: “Break-ins usually don’t start at the front door. Unlocked side gates or garages present vulnerable access points often left unmonitored by homeowners. […] We built these sensors because the perimeter of a home deserves the same protection as the inside of it.” Abode’s new Garage Tilt Sensor has a suggested retail price of $34.99, while the Outdoor Contact Sensor has a suggested retail price of $49.99. Comments

item.title: New Adobe plugin in ChatGPT combines Photoshop, Firefly, Premiere, Acrobat, and more
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 5.36
Adobe is unifying its ChatGPT integrations into a new plugin with more than 70 tools spanning photo editing, video, design, and PDFs. Here are the details. New Adobe plugin in ChatGPT available today Last year, we covered the launch of Adobe’s first native integrations with ChatGPT, which brought features from Photoshop, Adobe Express, and Acrobat directly into the chatbot. With these integrations, users could edit images, create and animate designs, and manage, merge, or modify PDFs directly within ChatGPT. Today, the company is combining its previously separate ChatGPT connectors into a single Adobe plugin in ChatGPT, available across ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, and Codex. Once activated, users can describe the result they need and let the Adobe plugin orchestrate more than 70 tools across the company’s creative and productivity suites to create it. Here’s Adobe: “ (…) the Adobe plugin in ChatGPT supports a wide range of workflows, from editing photos and creating campaign videos to designing marketing assets and generating polished PDFs — all through rich, interactive experiences right in the flow of the conversation. That breadth of capabilities means the plugin can adapt to the needs of your project, and when you want advanced editing, creative control or pixel-level precision, you can continue your work in Adobe’s apps right where you left off.” According to Adobe, the unified plugin includes the capabilities previously available through its ChatGPT integrations, along with additional tools drawn from Adobe Express, Photoshop, Firefly, Premiere, Acrobat, Lightroom, Illustrator, InDesign, Adobe Stock, and more. Today’s launch is part of a broader expansion of Adobe’s tools across AI platforms, including ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot, with integrations for Slack and Gemini set to follow later this month. Here are some examples of how users can leverage the new Adobe plugin in ChatGPT: - Create high-quality creative for your campaign: Upload your campaign photos and describe the look you want. The Adobe plugin applies a consistent style across the entire set, saves the finished assets to Creative Cloud and transforms your strongest image into a product or packaging mockup. - Create eye-catching video for every social platform: Turn a long-form video into an eye-catching highlight reel, then adapt it for YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels and other social platforms - Create a design and share it anywhere: Browse thousands of design templates with interactive previews, select the best one for your project, customize the copy and colors, then animate it for social media or convert it into a polished PDF that’s ready to share or print. - Transform data into customer-ready documents: Upload a spreadsheet or dataset and describe the result you need. The Adobe plugin transforms your information into professionally formatted PDFs, including event badges, catalogs, infographics and other customer-ready documents. Users can install the Adobe plugin by searching for Adobe in ChatGPT’s plugins directory. Once installed, it can be invoked by typing @Adobe in a prompt or selecting it from the + menu alongside other connected plugins. Adobe recommends that users sign in to their Adobe accounts “to unlock generative capabilities, access your Creative Cloud files, and save your work across sessions,” although guest access is also available. To learn more about the new Adobe plugin in ChatGPT, follow this link. Comments

item.title: Old Reddit a threat to AI data scraping, says platform, with changes coming
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 5.32
When Reddit significantly changed its user interface way back in 2018, there were widespread protests from those who preferred the original. The company has retained access to this at old.reddit.com, and last year promised this version would continue to exist for as long as people kept using it. That promise may now be under some degree of threat as Reddit says that it “plans to make changes” to Old Reddit in order to protect against AI data scraping … Upcoming changes to Old Reddit Reddit already made a big change to help fight AI when it started introducing account verification procedures. But the company now says it needs to do more, and that this will involve changes to Old Reddit. In order to protect our platform, business, and users from abusive scraping and spamming, over time we plan to make changes involving Old Reddit, the legacy desktop web experience for Reddit that was built 21 years ago. The news post is brief and vague, stating that the first change we’ll see is a requirement to be logged-in while using it, and hinting at moderators being required to use the new AI. In the short term, we will continue to require users to be logged in to access it and will work on migrating critical bots and moderator workflows to our modern stack. Beyond this, however, we don’t know what else may be in store for those who persist in using the older UI. CEO Steve Huffman promised last year that Old Reddit wasn’t going away, but how much of it will survive remains to be seen. AI moderation tools expanding Reddit has also announced that more AI moderation tools will be used to help fight spam, abuse and rule breaking as it expands tests of its automated Rules Hub. We’re expanding our test of Rules Hub, a suite of new moderation tools. With Rules Hub, moderators will be able to choose which rules should be automatically enforced, decide what happens when a rule is triggered (send to queue, filter, or remove), preview the experience before enabling it, and review logs and insights to understand how community rules are performing. The platform says this approach is likely to be more effective than older auto-moderation tools that rely on exact keyword matching. Comments

item.title: Lutron Caseta expands hands-free smart home controls through Sonos
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 5.25
Lutron is expanding its existing Caseta integration with Sonos, adding the ability to control smart-home devices using Sonos Voice Control. Sonos Voice Control for Lutron expands Beginning today, Caseta users can say “Hey Sonos” to control connected lights and shades from a voice-enabled Sonos speaker. Supported commands include turning lights on or off, changing their brightness, raising or lowering shades, checking device status, and activating Lutron scenes. The important distinction is that Lutron and Sonos already worked together. Caséta users could previously use a Pico audio remote to play or pause music, skip tracks, and adjust volume, while Lutron scenes could coordinate lighting, shades, and music. What’s new is control in the other direction: Sonos speakers can now serve as a hands-free interface for Caséta devices. Sonos Voice Control added broader Lutron support on July 20, initially covering the company’s HomeWorks and RadioRA 3 systems. Caseta and RadioRA 2 Select were listed as coming soon at the time. These voice requests are processed locally on compatible Sonos speakers. The integration requires a Lutron Smart Hub and a Sonos product with microphone support. Users can set it up from the Integrations section of the Lutron app. Sonos says Lutron home-control commands are currently available in US English. Do more with your Apple products Comments

item.title: Report: iPad shipments fell 8% in Q2 2026 amid global tablet market decline
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 5.03
Last week, Apple reported a 5% year-over-year drop in iPad revenue for the June quarter. Now, a new report puts that decline into the context of the broader tablet market’s performance for Q2 2026. Here are the details. Tablet shipments slide worldwide According to a new report published by research firm Omdia (via MacMagazine), worldwide tablet shipments fell to 35.5 million units during Q2 2026, marking a 9.9% drop year-over-year. For the first time in years, tablet shipments also defied the typical seasonal pattern of sequentially higher Q2 shipments driven by back-to-school demand. The report noted that despite a 7.5% drop in shipments, Apple still comfortably led the market, shipping 13.5 million iPads for a 37.8% share. Samsung followed with 5.8 million shipments and a 16.3% share, ahead of Lenovo at 11.1%, Xiaomi at 8%, and Huawei at 7.7%. Lenovo was the only top-five vendor to post growth, with shipments jumping 27.1% from Q2 2025. Omdia noted that vendors outside the top five collectively accounted for 19.1% of shipments, with their combined volume falling 23.5% year over year. Here’s Omdia’s Research Manager, Himani Mukka, on the report: “The past quarter saw one of the steepest declines in the tablet market over the past two years. (…) While the slowdown was anticipated, the market had remained more resilient than expected in prior quarters. Tablets have become an integral part of many households, and in several consumer use cases, detachable tablets are increasingly replacing traditional PCs for everyday computing. Relative affordability, the growing availability of larger-screen models, and tablets’ established role in education and field-based commercial environments continue to support important pockets of demand despite the broader market weakness.” Mukka added that, amid ongoing component supply constraints, “vendors are unlikely to broadly prioritize the tablet category.” Instead, they are expected to focus “their limited resources on flagship and premium models, further shifting their portfolios toward premium devices.” To read Omdia’s full report, follow this link. Comments

item.title: WhatsApp channel admins will soon get the ability to flag AI-generated media
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 4.99
As the EU’s new transparency requirements for AI-generated content take effect, WhatsApp is working on a feature that will allow channel admins to label certain types of AI-generated content. Here are the details. ’Channel admins in your country are required to label channel updates that use AI content’ As spotted by WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is working on a feature that will allow channel admins to label certain types of content as AI-generated. References to the new feature are currently found in WhatsApp’s latest Android beta, but since it appears to be a response to country-specific regulatory requirements, an iOS version and broader rollout are likely to follow. According to the report, the new feature will follow the same process used when channel admins run sponsored content: After sharing an update that contains AI-generated media, the admin can tap and hold the message to open the context menu. Here, there will be a new option called “Add AI content label”. This action adds a visible label to the message bubble, so followers can immediately see that the media was generated using artificial intelligence. After adding the AI label, users may not be able to remove it. WABetaInfo notes that not all AI-generated content will necessarily require labeling. As the current splash screen describes, AI content includes images, videos, or other media created or edited using AI tools. In other words, it appears that admins will not be required to label AI-generated text. It is currently unclear whether this option will be released worldwide or made available only where this type of labeling is required by law. To read WABetaInfo’s full report, follow this link. Comments

item.title: Siri AI is coming to newer Apple devices only, here’s the full list
item.description:

Siri AI is a major upgrade and highlight of iOS 27, macOS Golden Gate, and more. But only newer Apple devices will support the overhauled Siri. Here’s the full list of Siri AI-compatible hardware across iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, and Apple Vision Pro. Here are the Apple products that will support Siri AI when it launches iOS 27 and its companion updates will bring the major Siri overhaul we’ve been waiting for. Siri AI is currently in beta and will launch to the public this fall. But Siri AI will only be available on compatible hardware. Aside from upcoming devices like iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra, here is every current Apple product that supports Siri AI. iPhone - iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max - iPhone Air - iPhone 17 - iPhone 17e - iPhone 16 Pro and Pro Max - iPhone 16 and 16 Plus - iPhone 16e - iPhone 15 Pro and Pro Max iPad - iPad Pro (M1 chip and later) - iPad Air (M1 chip and later) - iPad mini (A17 Pro) Mac - All models with Apple silicon (M1 chip and later, and A18 Pro chip) Apple Watch (when paired with AI-supported iPhone) - Apple Watch Series 9 and later - Apple Watch Ultra 2 and later - Apple Watch SE 3 Apple Vision Pro - All models All of the products above will support Siri AI when it launches. For example, the ability to fully customize the pace and expressivity of Siri AI’s voice is only available on select hardware: iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17 Pro Max, iPhone Air, iPad models with M4 and later and at least 12GB of unified memory, Mac models with M3 and later and at least 12GB of unified memory, and Apple Vision Pro (M5) Additionally, Apple’s most powerful on-device AI model is restricted to a similar list of newer products. It’s unclear what impact that will have on Siri, though. Will Siri AI motivate you to upgrade to newer Apple hardware? Let us know in the comments. Comments

item.title: OpenAI asks for Apple’s trade secrets lawsuit to be dismissed, says it was filed without ‘adequate investigation’
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 4.77
The ongoing Apple-OpenAI lawsuit of alleged trade secrets theft continues, with OpenAI today filing a motion to have the case dismissed by a federal judge. OpenAI said Apple’s complaint was “filed without adequate investigation” and framed “ordinary conduct” out of context. Meanwhile, Apple is currently pressing for a preliminary injunction, which will be heard in court on October 1. The larger case could take years to resolve. In the motion to dismiss, OpenAI is attempting to have the whole thing thrown out early. It argues that Apple failed to meet the legal standard of presenting that it has tangible trade secrets, or that Apple failed to plausibly allege any improper conduct. It says that Apple’s examples of former employees discussing confidential information was mischaracterised. It references iMessage conversations that it also posted on its website earlier this week. OpenAI says these messages show that Chang Liu, one of the people named in the original suit, was asked by Apple employees to retrieve information, not that he was doing so for OpenAI’s benefit. It says Apple “does not allege that Mr. Liu ever disclosed a file to OpenAI or used one in OpenAI’s hardware work”. Similarly, the motion to dismiss addresses Apple’s comments that former-Apple VP Tang Tan retained a document describing Apple’s offboarding procedures. Apple alleged this document was used by Tan to aid evading various security checks when recruiting Apple employees. In OpenAI’s motion today, it frames it in the opposite fashion: suggesting that Tan used this information to ensure that any new employees he hired strictly followed Apple’s offboarding process to ensure that there was no chance of misconduct. Of course, all of this legalese is par for the course. We don’t know yet if OpenAI’s arguments meet the required legal standard for dismissal, but we aren’t surprised they are trying to get the complaint thrown out. That is the job of attorneys. At least right now, neither OpenAI nor Apple seem keen to settle the case. The next big milestone in proceedings will probably be the preliminary injunction hearing on October 1st. Comments

item.title: Apple prepares for iPhone 18 Pro and Ultra launch by expanding its reach
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 4.69
Apple is gearing up for a more focused and potentially much more expensive iPhone launch this fall. For starters, the cheaper base iPhone 18 is being saved for spring. That leaves the more expensive Pro models and Apple’s first foldable iPhone Ultra to carry September, with higher-than-usual starting prices expected. Here’s how Apple is already preparing to make the sticker shock more palatable for new customers and upgraders. Apple Upgrade lowers the monthly price First, Apple launched its new Klarna-backed Apple Upgrade program in July. Customers can lease an iPhone for either 12 or 24 months. The resulting monthly payment is lower than traditional financing over the same period because it covers only part of the device’s full price. At the end of the lease, customers can upgrade, return the iPhone, or pay the remaining balance to own it. AppleCare costs extra, but AppleCare One makes bundling warranties more affordable. Apple Upgrade gives the company a more approachable monthly number to advertise alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra. That matters when one of those phones could reportedly cost as much as $2,500, putting it in MacBook Pro territory. Apple raises iPhone trade-in values Next, just today Apple has increased trade-in values across most of its lineup. An iPhone 16 Pro Max now fetches up to $720, compared with $695 before. Meanwhile, the iPhone 16 Pro made a larger jump from $560 to $630. Customers can apply that credit toward either a traditional purchase or an Apple Upgrade lease. As a result, a higher trade-in value can reduce the monthly lease payment even further. Once the new iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra are officially announced in September, Apple should accept current iPhone models for trade-in as well. Apple expands Android trade-in eligibility Finally, Apple is making a direct play for Android switchers. Its updated list adds more models from Google, Samsung, and OnePlus. That includes the Pixel 9 lineup, Galaxy S21 Ultra, OnePlus 13, and OnePlus 13R. Those customers can apply their trade-in credit toward a purchase or Apple Upgrade lease as well. In other words, Apple is widening the entrance to its ecosystem just as its newest devices move further upmarket. None of these measures makes the iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone Ultra cheaper. Instead, they lower the visible monthly payment, increase the value of existing devices, and give more Android owners a way in. Together, those changes could make Apple’s most expensive iPhone launch easier to sell. For customers looking to upgrade without the larger sticker price, the standard iPhone 18 and cheaper iPhone 18e are due around March or April next year. Do more with your Apple products Comments

item.title: OpenAI updating ChatGPT with a smarter GPT-5.6 Sol and unlimited free chats
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 4.60
ChatGPT has become so much more than just chat over the last year. To that end, OpenAI is removing limits on text chat. ChatGPT will also improve with a smarter version of GPT-5.6 Sol. Details below. GPT-5.6 Sol gets smarter in ChatGPT OpenAI introduced GPT-5.6 Sol in June as the flagship member of a three-model family. Sol, Terra, and Luna became widely available in ChatGPT and Codex the following month. Now OpenAI is releasing a version of GPT-5.6 Sol tuned specifically for everyday conversations in ChatGPT. The company says the update should produce more focused answers, adapt the level of detail to each question, and avoid unnecessary formatting. The updates to GPT‑5.6 Sol in ChatGPT are designed to give you more direct responses, use tighter formatting, and avoid extra detail when it does not help. For a quick question, that means a direct answer with the context you need. For more involved work like multi-step planning, research or writing, it means a fuller response that keeps the main recommendation clear. The update also unifies ChatGPT’s Instant and Thinking experiences for Plus and Pro subscribers. Both will use GPT-5.6 Sol, with a new slider controlling how much thought the model puts into its response. The slider will be available across the ChatGPT apps for web, mobile, and desktop. Users can keep it low for quick questions or increase the reasoning level for research, planning, writing, coding, and more complicated decisions. Plus and Pro users can use the new slider in ChatGPT on web, mobile, and desktop to choose how much thought ChatGPT puts into an answer. Keep it quick for everyday questions, or move the slider up for planning, research, writing, coding, or decisions that need more thought. OpenAI also claims the revised model is more reliable when answering questions involving dates, numbers, rules, sources, and assumptions. In an internal evaluation covering financial, medical, and legal prompts, answers containing at least one factual error were reportedly 68% less common with GPT-5.6 Sol than with GPT-5.5 Instant. Unlimited ChatGPT text chats for free users The other major change applies to people using ChatGPT without a paid subscription. We’re expanding access to our latest models for free users with unlimited text chats using GPT‑5.6 Luna, plus a new Think button for harder questions. For questions that require deeper reasoning, Free users can tap the new Think button to give GPT‑5.6 Luna more time to work through the answer. Plus and Pro subscribers can begin using the revised GPT-5.6 Sol and reasoning slider today. This update only applies to the model used for regular ChatGPT conversations. OpenAI says the GPT-5.6 Sol version powering ChatGPT Work and Codex is not changing as part of this release. 9to5Mac’s Take Removing limits on text chat in ChatGPT is especially useful right now as Apple prepares to launch Siri AI in iOS 27 and macOS Golden Gate. Apple is essentially making text-based chat part of the core OS experience. However, Apple isn’t tackling many of the agentic features that modern ChatGPT offers. Making text chat unlimited matches what the platforms are able to offer as well. One more detail: Apple does say that some heavy Siri AI usage will require a paid iCloud+ account. ChatGPT removing limits on text chat potentially puts it ahead in this way. Do more with your Apple products Comments

item.title: In new court filing, Apple flags delays in Jon Prosser’s response to leak lawsuit
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 4.42
In a joint status report filing, Apple said it hadn’t heard from Jon Prosser’s lawyer in a month, which his counsel attributed to Prosser caring for his newborn child. Here are the details. Prosser’s discovery process hits delays Last year, shortly after announcing iOS 26, Apple sued Jon Prosser over videos in which he leaked the Liquid Glass redesign. Apple accused Prosser, alongside Michael Ramacciotti, of misappropriating trade secrets and violating the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act by accessing an Apple employee’s development iPhone and using its contents to publish the leaks. Based on court documents filed since then, Ramacciotti promptly cooperated with Apple’s discovery requests, while Prosser failed to formally respond to the lawsuit. Prosser would go on to deny this characterization. That said, this led the court to grant Apple’s request to enter default against him, which essentially meant he could no longer contest Apple’s allegations unless the default was set aside. Last June, Prosser’s lawyer filed a request to set aside the default, arguing that this would be the most efficient way to move the case forward. The court granted the request, kicking off an initial round of discovery in which Prosser provided Apple with documents and communications and sat for a deposition. However, in a joint status report filed yesterday, Apple says that there has been limited progress since then, which his counsel attributed to the birth of the leaker’s second child. From the filing: Apple and Mr. Prosser have worked to advance this case through limited discovery. Mr. Prosser provided documents and communications to Apple, and sat for a deposition on June 16, 2026. Unfortunately, Apple last heard from Mr. Prosser’s counsel on July 6th, 2026, despite repeated attempts to communicate and follow up on outstanding discovery issues. There still appear to be deficiencies in Mr. Prosser’s productions, and Apple has notified Mr. Prosser’s counsel of those issues. Shortly before this joint status update was to be filed, Mr. Prosser’s counsel explained that this delay in response may be due to the fact that Mr. Prosser just had a second child and is attending to the care of a newborn. Mr. Prosser’s counsel indicated that he will find dates when additional discovery may be provided to Apple. The report, signed by attorneys for Apple, Ramacciotti, and Prosser, adds that Ramacciotti has agreed to supplement his interrogatory responses and sit for a second deposition in September, and that the parties expect to file another status update on October 7. You can read the full filing below: Comments

item.title: X Money FAQ: Account suspensions, 6% APY, physical cards, and more
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 4.19
Following X Money’s launch last month, one question has repeatedly surfaced: What happens to your money if X suspends or closes your social media account? What happens to X Money if your X account gets banned? The short answer is that, in most cases, nothing happens. According to X’s updated suspension policy, users suspended for policies other than Child Safety or Violent and Hateful Entities violations will retain access to every X Money feature “with no interruption.” For suspensions involving either of those two policies, X says access to Money will be revoked and the remaining balance will be returned by check. In other words, X says an account suspension won’t result in your money being forfeited. Why would anyone use X Money? The most compelling answer is its interest rate. Premium+ subscribers currently earn 6% APY on eligible balances. Premium subscribers receive 4%, increasing to 6% after at least $1,000 in qualifying direct deposits (including payroll or X Creator payouts) within the preceding 34 days. That compares favorably with many leading online savings accounts, which are currently clustered around 4%. It also substantially exceeds the 3.5% APY currently offered by Apple Card Savings. The calculation is less attractive if you subscribe to X solely for the higher rate. But for existing Premium or Premium+ customers, it is a competitive place to hold cash. Eligible X Card purchases also receive 3% cash back. Is X Money a bank? X Payments itself is not an FDIC-insured bank. Deposit accounts are provided by Cross River Bank, Member FDIC, with the standard $250,000 coverage. An optional sweep program distributes larger balances among participating banks and is designed to provide as much as $10 million in total FDIC coverage, although X notes that individual placements are not guaranteed to remain below each bank’s insurance limit. What about the X Card? Every customer receives a virtual Visa debit card that can be added to Apple Pay. Physical metal cards are now reaching early customers as well. The physical card does not print its number, expiration date, or security code. Customers can customize how their name appears and may include their X handle, but neither the handle nor a full name is required. Initials are allowed if you don’t want to display your full name. The virtual and physical cards also use separate card numbers. How does this compare with Apple? Apple Card Savings remains operated by Goldman Sachs for now, but the broader Apple Card program is moving to JPMorgan Chase over roughly two years. The key difference is that Apple Card offers a credit card. X Money offers a debit card with a savings feature. Chase reportedly intends to offer a new Apple savings account. Existing customers are expected to be given a choice between keeping their Goldman Sachs savings account or opening the eventual Chase version. Apple has not announced what interest rate Chase will offer. You can learn much more about X Money here. Do more with your Apple products Comments

item.title: Biggest backdoor yet found in Chinese routers sold under multiple brand names
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 3.96
The most blatant security backdoor yet seen in an internet router has been found in a range of models sold under multiple brand names. A firmware implant phones home to cloud servers in China to ask for instructions, and can then be remotely controlled … Earlier this year, the US government banned the import and sale of all new models of Chinese routers, citing national security risks. It followed the discovery last year that thousands of Asus routers had been compromised by a botnet, with devices from Cisco, D-Link and Linksys also targeted. A major challenge to avoiding these kinds of embedded malware threats is that so many Chinese-made routers are sold under different brands, sometimes with different claimed countries of origin. Additionally, many are rebadged and supplied as standard by US ISPs, so customers have literally no idea who made their router. Cybersecurity company VulnCheck has now found an incredible and deliberate backdoor built into routers made by Shenzhen Zhibotong Electronics and sold under a variety of brands that include Zbtlink and Wiflyer. They dubbed it ENDLESSDOORS as it can be exploited in endless ways. They are an implant, a phone-home trojan horse. Our zero-day research team named this ENDLESSDOORS. This, at its core, is a small tool called rctl (remote control linux). Uploaded to GitHub on January 14, 2015 and never touched again, this obscure repository implements a simple command and control client and server. The server listens on port 7000 for clients to connect. It can send the client individual shell commands or tell the client to spawn a reverse bash shell. The researchers say that it poses the biggest risk yet seen because it initiates the contact with its command and control servers. Because the device dials out, none of this requires the router to be reachable from the internet. There’s no listening port to find and no inbound rule to punch through. The connection originates inside the network and traverses NAT and typical egress filtering the way any outbound TCP session does. A unit sitting behind three layers of firewall in a hotel back office is exactly as reachable as one with a public IP, provided it can get to the [command server]. How to check your router VulnCheck says you should ignore whatever branding your router may have and check for one of the affected model numbers: CPE2801, WE1026-5G-WD, WE1326, WE2007, WE2008-DSIM, WE2416, WE3326, WE5927, WE5931, WE5931AC, WE826-T3-DSIM, WG108, WG1602, WG1608-DSIM, WG209, WG2105, WG2107, WG259, WG3526, Z8102AX-2DSIM If your router is one of these, you should immediately disconnect and replace it. item.title: AirPods Pro 3 keep getting better, here’s what’s new in iOS 27
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 3.63
AirPods are getting a variety of new features in iOS 27, two of which are exclusive to AirPods Pro 3. Here’s everything new. Custom EQ Custom EQ is a feature that some AirPods users thought Apple would never ship. But it’s here in iOS 27, available now in the AirPods beta. With Custom EQ, Apple now lets you set your own sound profile for AirPods. Per Apple: AirPods are designed and engineered by Apple to faithfully represent music, TV shows and movies, and calls. If you prefer a different sound profile, you can customize how AirPods represent any audio played. You can change the EQ by going to your AirPods’ settings ⇾ Audio & Routing ⇾ Equalizer ⇾ Custom. From here, you can adjust the sound profile for low, mid, and high frequencies. Custom EQ is available on AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Max 2, and AirPods 4. GymKit can sync AirPods Pro 3’s heart rate data Apple GymKit has been available for years, but only for Apple Watch. It lets you pair and sync workout data with compatible cardio equipment, like treadmills, ellipticals, indoor bikes, and more. In iOS 27, GymKit expands to support iPhone using AirPods Pro 3’s heart rate sensor. My colleague Zac gave it a try: The setup is simple. I tapped my iPhone to the treadmill, picked Indoor Walk (Indoor Run is also offered), and started the workout from the treadmill. With GymKit, workout data is stored privately on iPhone and removed from the equipment. Once the workout started, the treadmill received heart-rate data from AirPods Pro 3. Meanwhile, the Fitness app on iPhone received the treadmill’s distance, pace, incline, and calorie data. Treadmills know details that an iPhone and AirPods can’t know on their own, especially incline and precise belt distance. For more details on iOS 27’s GymKit feature for AirPods Pro 3, check out Zac’s full hands-on below. Read more: iOS 27 basically turns your iPhone and AirPods into an Apple Watch at the gym Siri AI For most AirPods users, the single biggest upgrade in iOS 27 will be Siri AI. Siri AI is available on compatible iPhone hardware in iOS 27, and Apple made sure to expand full support for the AI assistant to AirPods too. AirPods are essentially becoming an AI wearable thanks to the new Siri. It will let users do a lot more than the current Siri. Here are some key features via Apple’s website: - World Knowledge: “Ask about virtually any topic that’s on your mind, from important facts to recipes and restaurant recommendations. Siri AI can reference information online to give you detailed, up-to-date insights.” - Conversational: “Siri AI is your conversational AI assistant with entirely new capabilities…Ask open-ended questions, brainstorm ideas for work or creative projects on the go, and engage in natural, back-and-forth conversations.” - Personal Context: “Siri AI can find relevant answers to what you’re looking for just by asking. Search for a photo from years ago, easily locate an email buried in your inbox, or pull up a note you saved on your iPhone.” Read more: AirPods keep getting better, and iOS 27’s biggest upgrade is Siri Precision Finding via Apple Watch Earlier this year when AirTag 2 launched, Apple brought Precision Finding support to Apple Watch for the first time. Until now though, it’s been limited to AirTag 2. But with iOS 27 and watchOS 27, Apple expands Precision Finding on the Watch to AirPods Pro 3. AirPods Pro 3’s case includes the latest second-generation Ultra Wideband (UWB) chip, letting you find it with greater precision and step-by-step guidance right from your wrist. Redesigned Settings menus With every batch of new AirPods features that debuts, the AirPods settings screen in the Settings app gets more cluttered. But in iOS 27, Apple has a welcome fix: it’s redesigned and reorganized all AirPods settings. Now, you’ll find AirPods settings organized into more categories and submenus, accompanied by colorful icons. It makes finding the right setting way easier and more intuitive than before. Read more: iOS 27 revamps AirPods settings in a big way, here’s the new design Which new AirPods features in iOS 27 are you most excited about? Let us know in the comments. item.title: Vision Pro is a niche product, but an incredibly valuable one in the right hands
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 3.53
Even Apple CEO Tim Cook has acknowledged that Vision Pro is a niche product. I’ve argued in the past that it’s an essential step along the way to a more affordable and consumer-friendly Apple Glasses product. But it’s also worth noting that sometimes niche products can make a huge difference within specialist fields, and a new surgical study provides a very clear example of why it matters to patients and surgeons alike … Growing use of Vision Pro for surgery Endoscopic surgery is performed using tiny instruments passed through a thin tube, with the surgeon relying a camera feed to a monitor in the operating room. Operating in this way requires a much smaller incision, significantly reducing recovery times for patients. A number of surgeons have switched out the monitor for a Vision Pro headset. We first saw this more than two years ago, when a renowned neurosurgeon used it for multiple spine reconstruction surgeries. Others have said that it can reduce pain and discomfort for surgeons and even reduce their risk of injury. The headset has also been used by other members of a surgical team, including a senior scrub nurse, who described it as eliminating human error when anticipating which tools a surgeon would need to use next. The device has also been used to help surgeons plan and visualise operations that are subsequently carried out using a surgical robot, as well as assisting visualization during conventional procedures. And while that $3,500 price tag is an expensive one for consumers, it’s actually very cheap when compared to the conventional monitors used in operating rooms, which run to $20,000 each. ‘Faster and better’ Analyst Horace Dediu contributed to a peer-reviewed UC San Diego study demonstrating the value of Vision Pro for surgeons. It found that swapping out a conventional monitor for a Vision Pro headset had multiple benefits for surgeons and patients alike. The study compared surgery carried out with traditional monitors with those using Vision Pro, finding multiple benefits. • 19% shorter operative times • 100% functional success with no intraoperative or postoperative complications • Significantly lower surgeon-reported workload, with every participating surgeon preferring the Apple Vision Pro experience • Improved ergonomics, allowing surgeons to maintain a natural, forward-facing posture So yes, Vision Pro is a development tool that helps pave the way for true consumer products – but it also has significant value in its own right in the right hands. Photo: Apple Comments

item.title: A live iPhone launch seems unlikely, but the event could be live-lier this year
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 3.48
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman stirred things up a little with what was likely a deliberately teasingly-phrased tweet. Some took this to be a reference to a live iPhone keynote presentation instead of a pre-recorded one. That seems unlikely, but there are a couple of reasons for suspecting that the live elements may be livelier this year … From live presentations to hybrid format Apple’s keynote presentations and iPhone launches famously used to be carried out live on stage. The pandemic saw Apple forced to abandon the live approach for WWDC 2020 in favour of pre-recorded video presentations – and the company apparently liked the results as it’s used pre-recorded video segments for both WWDC keynotes and iPhone launches ever since. Of course, the live audiences returned, complete with Apple execs appearing on stage to introduce some of the recorded segments, which delivered a hybrid experience. My own view is that this provides the best of both worlds: the excitement of live reactions and stage presence coupled to slicker and better-paced presentations. We saw Apple take another step in this hybrid direction at this year’s WWDC, with a live Tech Talk panel straight after the keynote. - Craig Federighi details Apple’s collaboration with Google for Siri AI in iOS 27 - Apple explains why Siri’s major iOS 27 overhaul took so long - Craig Federighi explains why Apple made a Siri chatbot app after all That ‘in-person’ phrase Gurman then wrote a story about a retail employee lottery to attend the event, and seemingly chose deliberately teasing phrasing for the accompanying tweet. A number of people took the “in-person” phrasing to mean a live presentation. In reality, of course, there have always been Apple staff in attendance to help run the event, performing tasks like organizing the lines, checking in guests, offering directions, and assisting with the hands-on demos. That’s almost certainly all that is meant here. Likely not live, but livelier Some have suggested that John Ternus taking over from Tim Cook could see a shake-up in the format, but personally I think the opposite is more likely the case. Live presentations always carry some risk of demo failure or other mishap, and it would be a massive risk for Ternus to have a live presentation during his debut as CEO. However, I do think that the live elements of this year’s event could be more animated, for two reasons. First, the iPhone Ultra will be one of the biggest changes to the iPhone lineup since the launch of the iPhone X. If Apple does a live panel following the video presentations as it did at WWDC, then there is likely to be a lot of excitement in the room. With the device itself officially unveiled, the company will also be free to talk more about the implications for iOS 27 and beyond. Second, Ternus has a significantly more relaxed style than Cook. That’s likely to create a different atmosphere, both in any live panel discussion and throughout informal interactions with attendees during the hands-on sessions. What’s your view? Do you think we may indeed see a live keynote presentation, or do you think Apple will stick to the existing hybrid format with perhaps a bit more of a human feel? Please take our poll and share your thoughts in the comments. Comments

item.title: CarPlay in iOS 27 adds two new features for popular Apple apps
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 3.39
CarPlay in iOS 27 has a handful of new features and improvements, including two additions for some of Apple’s most popular apps, like Apple Music and Apple Podcasts. CarPlay gives audio apps in iOS 27 new MiniPlayer and audio scrubbing features Outside of navigation apps like Apple Maps, the most-used category of CarPlay apps is audio. Audio apps like Apple Music, Apple Podcasts, Spotify, Overcast, and more are essentials when you’re on the go. And in iOS 27, Apple has two improvements coming for your favorite audio apps: - MiniPlayer - Audio scrubbing When using a CarPlay audio app, previously the top-right corner had a waveform icon you could tap to open the Now Playing screen. But in iOS 27, that waveform has been replaced by a new MiniPlayer. The MiniPlayer features artwork for whatever’s currently playing and offers play/pause and skip controls. Thanks to this change, you can access basic playback controls while browsing other parts of the app outside of Now Playing. Audio scrubbing is new to CarPlay in iOS 27 too. iPhone users are well accustomed to scrubbing through audio or video by tapping and dragging the playhead. But that’s never been supported in CarPlay before now. In iOS 27 though, the playhead has increased in size and now supports scrubbing to quickly navigate through a podcast, audiobook, or song. These changes apply to Apple’s own CarPlay apps, but they should also extend to most third-party audio apps once they’re updated for iOS 27 too. What additional audio app changes do you hope to see in CarPlay? Let us know in the comments. Comments

item.title: iPadOS 27 adds two new iPad features I’ve been loving
item.description:
Source: 9to5Mac Score: 3.33
iPadOS 27 launches next month, with new features in apps like Notes, Messages, Calendar, Mail, and more. Here are a couple of systemwide iPadOS 27 features I’ve been loving. #1: Menu bar and status bar improvements iPadOS 27 now lets you optionally keep the menu bar visible at all times In iPadOS 26, you had to swipe down from the top of the screen to reveal the menu bar, or alternately move your trackpad cursor to the top. This was fine, but it differed from the Mac’s persistent menu bar. Now iPadOS 27 lets you get more of that Mac-like experience. Inside Settings ⇾ Multitasking & Gestures there’s a new toggle: ‘Automatically Show and Hide Menu Bar.’ Make sure the toggle is off and the menu bar will stay visible at all times. Second, the name for your active app is now always visible too, included with the status bar in the top-left part of the screen. This is another way iPadOS 27 borrows from the Mac. Since the app name is in the status bar, it will be visible even if you opt to keep the menu bar hidden. Having the app name visible is especially helpful if you use keyboard shortcuts often, since shortcuts depend on the active app. #2: CMD + Space for Siri AI and Spotlight I keep my iPad Pro paired with a Magic Keyboard all the time, and while CMD + Space has always been useful, iPadOS 27 makes it more valuable than ever. That’s because the new Spotlight is not only better at search, it also bakes in Siri AI’s full capabilities. With a keyboard attached, it’s quick and convenient to ping Siri in an instant. I’ve found myself using CMD + Space all the time now that Siri is a full-fledged AI assistant. And I love that access to the full Spotlight feature set is accessible via the same shortcut. In my experience, iPadOS does a great job determining whether your query should ultimately be directed to Siri or Spotlight. So from a user standpoint, you don’t have to even think about it—just type. What are some of your top iPadOS 27 features and changes so far? Let us know in the comments. Comments
